questions.question: A clerk adds the alphabet ranks of distinct letters only; repeated occurrences are ignored. What number is assigned to BATHINDA?
A six-letter code reads original places 4,1,6,2,5,3. The code is NKLAAR. Which word was rearranged?
questions.explanation: Put N,K,L,A,A,R back at places 4,1,6,2,5,3 respectively. Reading original positions 1–6 gives KARNAL.

questions.question: Coordinates are row first, column second. Columns: 0 1 2; row 0: J A L; row 1: A M R; row 2: R L A. Which sequence correctly codes JAL?
questions.explanation: Read each pair separately: 00=J, 10=A and 21=L. Alternative A or L cells are allowed, but every pair must match.

questions.question: Base: A→2,E→5,I→8,N→%,R→7. Count vowels in the original input and apply ONLY the first matching rule: (1) exactly two vowels: replace both endpoint codes by #; (2) both endpoints vowels: reverse the full base code, then replace its middle code by @; (3) otherwise retain the base. Encode ANIRE.
questions.explanation: ANIRE has three vowels, so rule 1 fails and rule 2 applies. Reverse 2%875 to 578%2, then replace its middle code: 57@%2.

questions.question: Each word has one fixed code and token order is arbitrary: “farmers sell wheat” = “zu pa ni”; “traders buy wheat” = “ko ni re”; “farmers buy seeds” = “pa re lo”. Find the code for “sell seeds”.
questions.explanation: Common words identify wheat=ni, farmers=pa and buy=re. The remaining codes are sell=zu and seeds=lo.

questions.question: A ticket machine uses L→7, O→@, H→4, R→%, I→2. Which ticket prints for LOHRI?
questions.explanation: Replace letters in their original order: L O H R I → 7 @ 4 % 2.

questions.question: At a fair, real objects are renamed once: DRUM→FLUTE, FLUTE→FLAG, FLAG→LAMP. Simran actually picks up a FLUTE. Which code name must the announcer use?
questions.explanation: Follow the arrow from the real object FLUTE once. Its assigned name is FLAG.

questions.question: An encoder reverses a six-letter word, then applies +1,-2,+3,-4,+5,-6. Its output is FJSIJN. What was the input?
questions.explanation: Undo the shifts to recover E L P M E T in reverse order, then reverse to obtain TEMPLE.

questions.question: A label contains, in order, the middle letter of an odd-length word, its number of distinct letters, and its last letter moved +2. What is the label for PATIALA?
questions.explanation: PATIALA has middle letter I and five distinct letters P,A,T,I,L. The last A moves to C, giving I5C.

questions.question: In a fixed digit substitution, 248 is written as 591 and 826 as 157. What is the code for 6824?
questions.explanation: The pairs are 6→7, 8→1, 2→5 and 4→9. Hence 6824 becomes 7159.

questions.question: A name is encoded as two-digit alphabet ranks after every original letter moves +3 cyclically. Decode 17080816.
questions.explanation: Split into 17,08,08,16 to obtain QHHP. Move each letter back 3 places to get NEEM.

questions.question: A fixed one-to-one word code ignores order. “clean village roads” = “ti mu ka”; “village schools open” = “mu zo pe”; “clean schools shine” = “ti zo ra”; “roads shine daily” = “ka ra fu”. Which code set means “open clean daily”?
questions.explanation: The overlaps give clean=ti, village=mu, schools=zo and shine=ra. The unmatched words give open=pe and daily=fu, so use pe ti fu.

questions.question: A student’s name was encoded by moving every letter 5 places backward. The code is HPNFVI. Which original name was entered?
questions.explanation: Undo -5 with +5: H→M, P→U, N→S, F→K, V→A and I→N. The name is MUSKAN.

questions.question: Odd places move +3 and even places move -2, counting from the left. A coded surname is VGQEK. Recover the surname.
questions.explanation: Undo the alternating shifts with -3,+2,-3,+2,-3. VGQEK becomes SINGH.

questions.question: Use opposite alphabet pairs A↔Z, B↔Y, and so on. Which code represents JASS?
questions.explanation: Opposite ranks add to 27: J→Q, A→Z and S→H. Thus JASS becomes QZHH.

questions.question: In a seven-letter word, keep the middle letter fixed, move the final three letters to the front, and move the first three to the end without reversing either group. Code PUNJABI.
questions.explanation: Split PUNJABI as PUN | J | ABI. Exchanging the outer groups gives ABIJPUN.

questions.question: A single fixed shift changes JHELUM to MKHOXP. Which additional entry breaks this rule?
questions.explanation: Every letter moves +3. RAVI must become UDYL, so RAVI → UDYK is the incorrect entry.

questions.question: At place i, encoding adds i² to the alphabet rank and wraps within A–Z. Which original produces the code SMEUQ?
questions.explanation: Subtract 1,4,9,16,25 from successive letters. S→R, M→I, E→V, U→E and Q→R, giving RIVER.

questions.question: A number label lists each letter’s reverse alphabet value plus its place counted from the right, starting at 1. There is no numeric wraparound. Find the label for REWA.
questions.explanation: Reverse values are 9,22,4,26; add right-hand places 4,3,2,1. The label is 13-25-6-27.

questions.question: A one-to-one character mapping gives SEAT→$7@4 and EAST→7@$4. What does 4@$7 represent?
questions.explanation: From SEAT, 4=T, @=A, $=S and 7=E. Therefore 4@$7 decodes to TASE.

questions.question: A scanner repeats +2,-1,-1 across a whole string without restarting at spaces. It reads MOGA ROPAR. After spaces are removed, what are the last five coded letters?
questions.explanation: MOGA occupies places 1–4. Places 5–9 use -1,-1,+2,-1,-1, so ROPAR becomes QNRZQ.

questions.question: At a Patiala desk, every letter is moved 4 places forward in the alphabet, with Z followed by A. Which label replaces KIRAN?
questions.explanation: Add 4 to each letter: K→O, I→M, R→V, A→E, N→R. The code is OMVER.

questions.question: For a five-letter badge, the shift at place i is 2i, counting i=1 from the left. Select the badge code for NEPAL.
questions.explanation: Use shifts +2,+4,+6,+8,+10. NEPAL becomes PIVIV.

questions.question: Harpreet stores the complete name NABHA from right to left, keeping every letter. What is stored?
questions.explanation: Read NABHA from the final letter to the first: A-H-B-A-N.

questions.question: For a five-letter word, multiply the endpoint ranks, add the three inner ranks, then subtract the word length. What is the code of FORTS?
questions.explanation: Calculate 6×19 + (15+18+20) - 5 = 162. Multiply only the endpoint ranks.
